name: Basilica of St. Stanislaus
architect: Robert J. Reiley and Gustave E. Steinback
history: Polish immigrants who came to Chicopee's mills from the 1880s founded the parish in 1891, the first Polish parish in western Massachusetts; the first Mass was a midnight Mass at Christmas 1891 in an unfinished wooden church. Conventual Franciscans took charge in 1902. The present brownstone church was built in 1908, and John Paul II named it a basilica in 1991, the parish's centennial.
arch: A brownstone church by Reiley and Steinback of New York, with a pair of monumental masonry towers whose copper drums carry arched belvederes. It seats about 800 in a main nave and two side naves.
features: A pipe organ was installed in the choir loft in 1920.
European artists made its stained glass windows.

look.d: Each tower ends in a copper drum and an open belvedere.
The local brownstone gives the facade its warm color.

fun: Chicopee's Polish population grew from about 200 in 1885 to over 9,000 by 1914.
journal: Mill-town Poles built a cathedral-sized church. The towers still say so.
